known_limits: The physical candidate now reaches /init ready and answers help/echo on the real board twice: once with a volatile SOF configuration and once after a true power-cycle cold boot in which both the FPGA configuration and the payload came from EPCQ Flash.
The previous 16 MiB run is not a valid proxy for the 128 MiB board DDR and must not be used to sign off paging behavior.
The 128 MiB run progressed through page-table setup without external abort, but its timed WFIT loop has not been tied to a specific caller or GIC RWP read value.
The saved __delay caller LR was read from a stack line not resident in D-L1 and may be stale; original callsite still unverified.

The prior pre-patch run failed help RX because the generated JTAG-UART threshold required 56 queued bytes; the current target HDL and simulation model now assert after one byte, and the passing full-system regression consumes both commands.

The first printk NUL was traced to the Catapult write-back L1 zero-filling loads across a 64-byte line and dropping crossing-store tail bytes. Both paths are now split through the L1, the focused L1WB regression passes, and the current full Linux run has passed the prior corruption point.
The focused 128-byte cache/JTAG-UART test alone does not prove Linux; the later full-system simulation now independently proves EL0 /init and help/echo over JTAG-UART in the behavioral SoC model.

The focused core-integrated JTAG-UART test uses a synthetic printable source page and constant WSPACE=64. It proves basic LDRB/control-read/STR W traffic through the RTL bridge, but not the Linux init process, real RX syscalls, or vendor IP/CDC timing.

The first post-fit STA of the Linux candidate failed with a -103.394 ns sys_clk_25 setup violation (96-deep serial GIC priority scan). After the balanced-tree GIC fix the same flow reports +5.723 ns and TNR/TNS 0 everywhere; the earlier SOF from that failing run must not be used.

Writing the JIC needs the Serial Flash Loader helper design in the FPGA first; without it quartus_pgm stops with 'Flash Loader IP not loaded on device 1'. The recorded helper is helper_sofs/sfl_enhanced_10_02e060dd.sof.
The board transcripts contain nios2-terminal 'Gathering input from STDIO' noise whenever the terminal session runs without piped input; the *.clean.log files strip that line only.

The canonical production DTB does not pass swiotlb=, so Linux zeroes the default 64 MiB software IO TLB buffer during swiotlb_init. On the board that takes milliseconds, but in the behavioral simulation it is a long __memset that dominates the run (about 6.6 MB per 25M cycles, starting near cycle 325M). The earlier diagnostic DTB used swiotlb=1024 and therefore skipped most of this work; the two runs are not comparable after the first 325M cycles.

The GIC-tree RTL canonical-DTB full-Linux simulation was deliberately stopped at 775M cycles (of a 2B budget) to free the local resource lock for the Gate D rerun on the merge SHA. It had reached the SWIOTLB zeroing phase and was not diverging; the same RTL is proven on real hardware by the cold-boot transcript. The partial log is kept at build/agents/T-20260928-002/gic-tree-sim-20260930/simulation-stopped-at-775M.log.
next: Objective closed for this candidate. Remaining optional follow-up: finish the canonical-DTB 128 MiB behavioral simulation on the GIC-tree RTL (running under the local lock) as extra non-board evidence, and consider a second on-board command such as sleep/uptime.
